name: Beppu / Yufuin
days: 2 nights (together with friend), onsen ryokan stay
overview: The genuine slow-down stretch of the trip — 2 nights at an onsen ryokan rather than splitting a night with Fukuoka. Wants a hike/scenic viewpoint worked in (not purely low-key), and lodging needs to be tattoo-friendly with a private bath option.

recommendations.title: Mount Tsurumi + Beppu Ropeway
recommendations.summary: 1,375m peak, panoramic views, winter hoarfrost is a seasonal bonus.
recommendations.body: Panoramic views to Mount Yufu and the Kuju Mountains on a clear day. Ropeway up takes about 10 minutes (¥1,600-1,800 round trip) with a 15-minute walk to the actual summit; full hike up takes about 2-3 hours for a more demanding option. Given the ask for a real hike, doing the hike one way and the ropeway the other is a good balance. February timing bonus: winter (Dec-mid March) brings hoarfrost coating the trees near the summit in a crystalline ice layer — a seasonal effect specific to this time of year. Small shrine at the summit (Tsurumi Sanjo Gongen) adds a touch of traditional/historic. Wind-closure risk: February is a windier month and the ropeway closes irregularly in high wind — worth a backup plan.

recommendations.title: Mount Tsurumi hiking trail (wind backup)
recommendations.summary: Same mountain, same views, entirely on foot — unaffected by ropeway closures.
recommendations.body: Same mountain, same views, entirely on foot (base to summit and back, about 2-3 hours each way), unaffected by ropeway wind closures.

recommendations.title: Mount Yufu (Yufu-dake)
recommendations.summary: Standalone hike near Yufuin, twin-peak profile, no cable car involved.
recommendations.body: Recognizable twin-peak profile, no cable car involved at all so wind doesn't affect it. More physically demanding than Tsurumi (real elevation gain, exposed sections near the peaks) — worth checking the group's hiking fitness before committing.

recommendations.title: Kannawa hot spring district walk
recommendations.summary: Lower-key fallback if weather turns bad enough for neither hike.
recommendations.body: A scenic walking option through Beppu's steam-vented streets, for when weather turns uncooperative enough that neither mountain hike feels appealing.

recommendations.title: Jigoku Meguri (Hells Tour)
recommendations.imageQuery: Beppu Hells Tour hot spring ponds
recommendations.summary: Low priority — viewing-only tour of colorful boiling hot spring ponds.
recommendations.body: Viewing-only tour of colorful, boiling mineral hot spring ponds around Beppu (not for bathing). Rated "maybe, low priority" — slot as an if-time option on the lighter of the two days rather than planning around it.

recommendations.title: Yudofu and tofu-based dishes
recommendations.summary: Good vegetarian option, specialty of onsen towns like this.
recommendations.body: A specialty of onsen towns like this — good vegetarian option, unlike some of the meat-heavy specialties elsewhere on the trip. If a ryokan kaiseki dinner is included with lodging, flag the vegetarian requirement when booking; many can accommodate with advance notice.

recommendations.title: Tattoo-friendly, private-bath ryokan
recommendations.summary: Needs a private bath (kashikiri/kazoku-buro) option for tattoo-friendly bathing.
recommendations.body: Search for "kashikiri buro" or "kazoku-buro" (private family bath) as an amenity, or properties advertising "tattoo OK"/"irezumi OK" directly. Verify via Rakuten Travel or Jalan listings, or contact the property directly — policies can differ from what's listed online. Beppu has enough volume of tattoo-friendly options that this shouldn't meaningfully narrow choices; Yufuin has fewer, so worth double-checking there specifically.

openQuestions: Specific ryokan shortlist, filtered on tattoo-friendly + private bath + can accommodate vegetarian kaiseki
